definitions.explanation: A small, plump, short-tailed bird of grassland. In Japan it is best known for its small speckled eggs, which are eaten boiled in many everyday dishes.

examples.japanese: ウズラ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{茹|ゆ}でた→茹でる：02324_yuderu⟧。
{八宝菜|はっぽうさい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ウズラ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: Happosai has quail eggs in it.

examples.japanese: ウズラ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{小|ちい}さく→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧、⟦{草|くさ}むら→草むら：29900_kusamura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{隠|かく}れて→隠れる：02035_kakureru⟧⟦{暮|く}らしている→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: Quails are small and live hidden in the grass.

notes:
As with most animal names, usually written in katakana; the kanji is {鶉|うずら}. Hiragana うずら is common on food labels and menus.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ウズラ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧: quail egg — on skewers, in Chinese-style stir-fries ({八宝菜|はっぽうさい}), in oden and on top of some noodle dishes
- ウズラ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飼|か}う→飼う：08151_kau⟧: to keep quails

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan farms quail chiefly for eggs; the meat is much less common than in Europe.
